about: Vim drills for the eng major, checked by replaying keystrokes in real Vim: python3 scripts/vimcheck.py --drill topics/eng/vim-drills.json <id> "<keys>". One per lesson, following Practical Vim's tips; text comes from the 3D chess repos where possible. par = a good keystroke count (verified by the reference solution).

drills.tip: Practical Vim tip 1-2: the dot command
Practical Vim tips on text objects: change inner word

how_to_record: Record exactly what you type: `vim -W ~/keys.log drill.txt`, do the drill, finish with :wq. Then convert the recording to paste-able notation: `python3 scripts/vimkeys.py ~/keys.log` (or, without the repo: python3 -c "import sys;d=open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read();m={27:'<Esc>',13:'<CR>',10:'<CR>',9:'<Tab>',8:'<BS>',127:'<BS>',60:'<lt>'};print(''.join(m.get(b,'<C-%s>'%chr(b+96) if b<32 else chr(b)) for b in d))" ~/keys.log). The final :wq isn't counted.
